title: 'Sugar free' doesn't always mean zero
text: In Europe, a food can say 'sugar free' with up to 0.5 g of sugar per 100 g or 100 ml.
claim: A 'sugar free' claim is allowed if the product has no more than 0.5 g of sugars per 100 g or 100 ml.
queries: sugars-free claim no more than 0.5 g of sugars per 100 g or 100 ml

title: 'Zero calorie' drinks can still have a few
text: In Europe, a drink can be called energy-free with up to 4 kcal per 100 ml.
claim: An 'energy-free' claim is allowed for products with no more than 4 kcal per 100 ml.
queries: energy-free claim no more than 4 kcal per 100 ml

title: 'Fat free' allows a little fat
text: In Europe, 'fat free' means no more than 0.5 g of fat per 100 g or 100 ml.
claim: A 'fat free' claim is allowed if the product has no more than 0.5 g of fat per 100 g or 100 ml.
queries: fat-free claim no more than 0.5 g of fat per 100 g or 100 ml

title: 'Low sugar' has a number behind it
text: In Europe, 'low sugar' means at most 5 g per 100 g of food, or 2.5 g per 100 ml of drink.
claim: A 'low sugar' claim requires no more than 5 g of sugars per 100 g for solids or 2.5 g per 100 ml for liquids.
queries: low sugars claim no more than 5 g of sugars per 100 g solids 2.5 g per 100 ml liquids

title: 'No added sugar' can still be sweet
text: Fruit and milk have natural sugars. In Europe, such packs must say they contain naturally occurring sugars.
claim: Where sugars are naturally present in a product claiming 'no added sugars', the label must state that it contains naturally occurring sugars.
queries: no added sugars claim naturally occurring sugars should also appear on the label

title: The first ingredient is the biggest
text: Ingredients are listed by weight, largest first. If sugar comes second, there's more of it than most other things.
claim: Ingredients must be listed in descending order of their weight or volume.
queries: list of ingredients descending order of their composition by weight or volume FSSAI labelling
ingredients listed in descending order of weight food labelling regulation

title: Compare 'per 100 g', not 'per serving'
text: Serving sizes vary between brands. Indian labels give nutrition per 100 g or 100 ml (or per pack for small single-serve packs), so use that to compare.
claim: Nutritional information must be given per 100 g or 100 ml.
queries: FSSAI labelling nutritional information per 100 g or 100 ml or per serve
nutrition declaration expressed per 100 g or per 100 ml regulation

title: Green dot or brown triangle?
text: In India, a green dot in a square means vegetarian. A brown triangle in a square means non-vegetarian.
claim: Vegetarian food carries a green circle in a square and non-vegetarian food a brown triangle in a square.
queries: FSSAI vegetarian logo green colour filled circle non-vegetarian brown colour filled triangle

title: Not every number is a worry
text: Codes like INS 330 just name an additive. 330 is citric acid, the same acid that makes lemons sour.

title: Sodium isn't the same as salt
text: To get salt from sodium, multiply by 2.5. 400 mg of sodium is about 1 g of salt.
claim: Salt content is calculated as sodium multiplied by 2.5.
queries: salt means the salt-equivalent content calculated using the formula salt = sodium x 2.5

title: Look for 'trans fat' on fried snacks
text: In India, foods made with hydrogenated vegetable fat must say on the pack that they contain trans fats.
claim: Foods made with hydrogenated vegetable fats or bakery shortening must be labelled as containing trans fats.
queries: FSSAI hydrogenated vegetable fats bakery shortening label contains trans fats

title: Why some diet drinks mention phenylalanine
text: Aspartame contains phenylalanine, which people with the rare condition PKU must avoid, so labels have to warn them.
claim: Products containing aspartame must carry a statement that they contain phenylalanine, for people with phenylketonuria.
queries: aspartame label statement contains phenylalanine phenylketonurics

title: 'Use by' and 'best before' aren't the same
text: 'Use by' is about safety: don't eat it after that date. 'Best before' is about quality: it may just taste less fresh.
claim: A 'use by' date concerns safety, while a 'best before' date concerns quality.
queries: difference between use by date safety and best before date quality food
